title: Launch Cadence Harmonizer: Window Heatmap, OKR-Linked Prioritization, and Staggered Canary Plan
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce an executable launch calendar and slot-allocation plan that ties prioritized initiatives to OKR exposure, reserves capacity for runtime kernel/quantization rollouts, and defines staggered canary cohorts across runtime/console/API surfaces.

Why now: Upcoming runtime-1.22 includes kernel scheduling changes and a new batching heuristic that may shift latency tails for high-concurrency tenants. We need a launch plan that mitigates risk to latency SLAs while enabling phased capacity reservation for Dedicated customers and Private upgrade windows.

Deliverables:
- A launch heatmap (by region, surface, week) that maps initiative impact to OKR buckets and assigns slot priorities.
- Slot arbitration rules (preemptive/reserved/spot) + automated allocation spreadsheet.
- Canary cohort definitions + success criteria (latency P50/P95, error %, infra cost delta).
- Contingency lanes and fast-fallback policies (model variant fallback / routing policy changebook).
- Runbook for launch week, including owner roster, escalation matrix, and post-launch evaluation template.

Acceptance criteria:
- Stakeholder sign-off (Runtime, Console, API, SRE, Customer Success) on the heatmap and slot priorities.
- Simulated load run (see artifacts) shows no >10% increase in customer-facing P95 in canary cohort for runtime changes.
- Automation ready: slot allocation sheet wired to capacity signals (prelim mock endpoint).

Success metrics (post-launch 2 weeks):
- No customer-impacting incident related to kernel scheduling changes.
- <5% regression in tail latency across top 10 tenants.
- On-time rollout of 90% of initiatives in the release train without manual capacity overrides.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Kickoff: Reviewed with Runtime Eng (Lina Gomez) and SRE (Owen Park). Primary risk: KV cache invalidation behavior at scale after the kernel change. Action: Schedule focused perf benchmark for KV cache patterns.

2026-02-24 - PM sync: Decided to reserve two spot slots for Dedicated customers during Week 3. Rationale: gives buffer for burst traffic while minimizing long-term reservation cost. Follow-up: ENG-22412 to add slot tagging for dedicated vs spot.

2026-03-02 - Design review: Console team requested clearer visibility for slot owners and per-slot cost forecast. Created console mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ConsoleMock_preview (internal). Assigned DES-410 for visual refinement.

2026-03-05 - Trade-off note: We can either widen canary cohort (30% traffic) to reduce rollout time or narrow it (5%) to minimize risk. Decided on dynamic cohort ramp: start at 5%, step to 30% over 72 hours if SLOs hold. Documented ramp thresholds in runbook.

2026-03-08 - SRE feedback: Add automated health-check gating tied to trace error budget; if breached, auto-roll back to previous model variant and notify oncall. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/4123

2026-03-10 - Simulation results: Regional load sim for EU-West and us-east shows P95 latency delta +6% in worst cohort at peak QPS (details in artifact). Conclusion: proceed with Week 2 canary but enable additional cache warming preflight. Artifact: https://internal-dashboard.redwood.ai/sim/slot-101112

2026-03-12 - Stakeholder sign-off: Runtime, Console, and Customer Success approved heatmap and contingency lanes. Next: finalize owners in runbook and hand to Launch Conductor (Ops) for calendar commit.
